closure_explanation: Theorem 2 (Th1) is proved from Lemma 5 (Lm5) alone (line 445) plus the elementary induction on beta_k. Lemma 5's statement uses DOBOC-K (Algorithm 2 and the DOBOC-K distributed-implementation lemma, i.e. source Lemma 3, recorded as the algorithm node ALG), a = M + 2(1-w_min)/lambda, F and x_*; its proof uses the centralized form of DOBOC-K (an internal algebraic step), Proposition 1 (pp1, eigenvalue bounds of grad^2 F), Lemma 4 (Lm4) and the inequalities (mu), (L) via (key1), (key2) (internal derivations). Lemma 4 uses the Taylor expansion error of the C^2 local functions (DTAY, derived). Symmetry of grad^2 F (DSYM, derived) is implicit in the eigenvalue arguments. The minimum point x_* is presupposed (line 345); DMIN (derived) establishes its existence from (mu). DEXEC (derived) links the template execution (one oracle call per outer iteration) to the iterates. Excluded: Theorem 1 (superlinear rate of DOBOC, the K = k variant; not used by Theorem 2), Lemma 2 (Lm2, heuristic approximation motivating the algorithm), the DOBOC distributed-implementation lemma and Remark (hsf) (about DOBOC, not DOBOC-K), the optimal-control derivation (OCP, conlaw, iteration relation) and the citations [mokhtari2016network] (Proposition 1 is stated in the paper and formalized here), [apostol1991calculus] (Taylor expansion, formalized as DTAY), [mitrinovic2013classical] (Bernoulli inequality, an internal proof step). The only convergence result in the closure is Theorem 2; all other results are supporting. Fresh interface correction reuses the accepted mathematical dependency closure after new independent review, retaining the analytic theorem and its disclosed exponent correction. The public result derives a priori tuning and a logarithmic epsilon-budget, preserves the fixed inner-K method family, and measures one all-agent gradient/Hessian reply per outer update. It makes no unpenalized-consensus accuracy or primitive communication-count claim.

classification.reason: Problem formulation of Section 2: communication network and weight matrix shared by every result; contains only conditions, no claim.

clauses.justification: Section 2 node set; w_min = min_i w_ii requires at least one agent.
clauses.text: V = {1, ..., n} is a nonempty finite set of agents (n >= 1).
G is an undirected graph on V without self-loops; N_i is the set of neighbours of i; i and j can exchange messages iff they are adjacent.

clauses.justification: Section 2: 'a symmetric, doubly stochastic n x n matrix W'.
clauses.text: W is symmetric: w_ij = w_ji for all i, j.
W is doubly stochastic: every row sum and every column sum of W equals 1.
w_ij >= 0 for all i, j.

clauses.justification: Section 2; the equivalence is read for j != i because w_ii > 0 while i is not its own neighbour.
clauses.text: For i != j: w_ij = 0 iff j is not in N_i.
w_ii = 1 - sum_{j in N_i} w_ij and w_ii > 0 for every i.

interpretations.basis: Line 118 states w_ii = 1 - sum_{j in N_i} w_ij > 0 in the same sentence; a node is not its own neighbour (N_i is used together with N_i u {i}).
interpretations.decision: The clause 'w_ij = 0 iff j not in N_i' applies to off-diagonal entries.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Exactly the source network class; the diagonal is governed by the w_ii clause.

nodes.statement: Communication network: undirected graph G = (V, E), V = {1,...,n} (n >= 1 agents), neighbours N_i of node i; weight matrix W symmetric, doubly stochastic, entries w_ij >= 0, w_ij = 0 iff j is not a neighbour of i (for j != i), and w_ii = 1 - sum_{j in N_i} w_ij > 0. Agent i holds a local decision vector x^i in R^p; x = (x^1,...,x^n) in R^{np}.

classification.reason: Definitions of h, Z, the penalty function F and its gradient/Hessian expressions; no claim.

clauses.text: h(x) = sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x^i) for x = (x^1,...,x^n) in R^{np}.
Z = W (x) I in R^{np x np}; (Zx)^i = sum_j w_ij x^j = sum_{j in N_i u {i}} w_ij x^j (w_ij = 0 off N_i u {i}).
F(x) = h(x) + (1/(2 lambda)) x^T (I - Z) x.
grad F(x) = grad h(x) + (1/lambda)(I - Z) x, grad h(x) = (grad f_1(x^1), ..., grad f_n(x^n)).

clauses.justification: Line 204 defines grad^2 h; line 249 and the proof of Lemma 5 (line 399) use grad^2 F(x_k) = grad^2 h(x_k) + (I - Z)/lambda.
clauses.text: grad^2 h(x) = blockdiag(grad^2 f_i(x^i)); grad^2 F(x) = grad^2 h(x) + (1/lambda)(I - Z) as a linear map on R^{np}.

interpretations.basis: Line 129 gives grad F by this formula; line 249 calls grad^2 h(x_k) + (I - Z)/lambda the second-order information of F; grad^2 f_i is the Hessian of the C^2 function f_i (derivative of grad f_i).
interpretations.decision: grad F and grad^2 F are the explicit expressions above (the gradient and Hessian of F, F being h plus a quadratic form with symmetric matrix (I - Z)/lambda).
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Same objects as the source; no additional assumption.

interpretations.basis: x^T y and ||.|| on R^{np} with x = (x^1,...,x^n) stacked.
interpretations.decision: The Euclidean structure of R^{np} is the product L2 structure: <x, y> = sum_i <x^i, y^i>, ||x||^2 = sum_i ||x^i||^2.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Identical to the source vector space.

clauses.text: Every agent starts from x_0^i in R^p; inputs eta, lambda > 0 and K.
ghat_0^i = eta [grad f_i(x_k^i) + (1/lambda)(x_k^i - sum_{j in N_i u {i}} w_ij x_k^j)] using neighbour values x_k^j.

For t = 0, ..., K-2: ghat_{t+1}^i = eta [grad f_i(x_k^i) + (1/lambda)(x_k^i - sum_{j in N_i u {i}} w_ij x_k^j)] + (1 - eta/lambda) ghat_t^i - eta grad^2 f_i(x_k^i) ghat_t^i + (eta/lambda) sum_{j in N_i u {i}} w_ij ghat_t^j.
x_{k+1}^i = x_k^i - ghat_{K-1}^i; the iterates x_k, k = 0, 1, ..., are generated from x_0.

interpretations.basis: The proof (lines 456-461) needs beta_0 >= m^2 eta/a - (a^3 (2a)^{3/2} eta^3 K^3 L/(6m^3)) Delta^{1/2} > 0, i.e. eta^2 < 6 m^5/(a^4 (2a)^{3/2} K^3 L Delta^{1/2}); epsilon and (ddgx) carry (2a)^{3/2}. With the literal 2/3 the claim 0 < epsilon is false: n = 1, p = 1, W = [1], lambda = 1, f(x) = x^2 (m = M = a = 2), L = 1, K = 1, eta = 1/4, x_0 = 50 (Delta = 2500) satisfies (29) and the printed condition (1/16 < 6*32/(16 * 4^{2/3} * 50)), but epsilon = 3/4 - 50/48 < 0. Hence 2/3 is a typographical transposition of 3/2.
interpretations.decision: The exponent of (2a) in the step-size bound is 3/2 (the source prints 2/3 in the statement and at line 461).
interpretations.effect_on_scope: The formal condition is the one the source proof establishes; it is weaker than the printed one when 2a < 1 and stronger when 2a > 1, where the printed statement is false.

interpretations.basis: For eta > 0 and a positive denominator both forms are equivalent (squaring monotone on nonnegatives). When L = 0 or x_0 is a minimiser (Delta = 0) the printed fraction is undefined; the cleared form is then automatically true and the conclusion still holds (epsilon = (2m^2 eta - m a^2 eta^2 K^2)/a > 0 and the rate follows from Lemma 5 without the cubic term).
interpretations.decision: The condition eta < [6 m^5/(a^4 (2a)^{3/2} K^3 L Delta^{1/2})]^{1/2} is encoded as eta^2 * (a^4 (2a)^{3/2} K^3 L Delta^{1/2}) < 6 m^5 with Delta = F(x_0) - F(x_*).
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Covers the full source domain where the condition is defined, plus its definedness boundary where the conclusion remains true; no source case is dropped.

interpretations.decision: x_* is a minimum point of F, recorded as a parameter constrained by TH2/min; it exists by DMIN (used when the public Convergence packaging asserts existence). Delta = F(x_0) - F(x_*) in the step-size condition is evaluated at that point (the minimum value is unique, so the choice does not matter).
The headline quantity is the number of DOBOC-K iterations k (each iteration performs K-1 inner communication rounds); the rate holds for every k.

interpretations.basis: Network nonnegativity implies a<=A. The tuning implies eta<1, eta<1/a, eta*a^2*K^2/m<=1/2 and eta^2*a^4*(2a)^(3/2)*K^3*L*sqrt(actualGap)/(6m^5)<=1/4; hence all original corrected step conditions hold and rate(actualGap)>=m^2*eta/a>=rho>0. The source rate and (1-r)^N<=exp(-rho*N) give accuracy; when Delta<=epsilon the ceiling is zero and x0 already suffices.
interpretations.decision: Keep the existing arbitrary-eta, arbitrary-outer-horizon analytic theorem as a supporting library result. For the public accuracy wrapper supply known Delta >= F(x0)-F(xstar), epsilon > 0, and fixed inner communication depth K >= 1. Set A=M+2/lambda, C=1+A+A^2 K^2/m+sqrt(A^4 (2A)^(3/2) K^3 L sqrt(Delta)/(6m^5)), eta=1/(2C), rho=m^2/(2AC), and N=ceil(2AC/m^2 * log(max(1,Delta/epsilon))). Output the N-th stacked iterate with pointwise F(output)-F(xstar)<=epsilon. The minimizer is analysis-only and excluded from public information.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Derived explicit-complexity corollary for every original admissible objective and every fixed inner K, using known gap bound; raw theorem retains all originally accepted choices of eta and horizon. No assumptions on objectives or stronger topology are introduced. The previously accepted source exponent correction 2/3 to3/2 is retained and disclosed.

nodes.statement: Theorem 2: let x_k be generated by DOBOC-K. Under the network conditions, Assumptions 1 and 2, lambda > 0, eta > 0, K >= 1, (29) eta < min{1, 1/a, 2m/(a^2 K^2)} and eta < min{m/(a^2K^2), [6 m^5/(a^4 (2a)^{3/2} K^3 L (F(x_0) - F(x_*))^{1/2})]^{1/2}}, with epsilon = (2 m^2 eta - m a^2 eta^2 K^2)/a - (a^3 (2a)^{3/2} eta^3 K^3 L/(6 m^3)) (F(x_0) - F(x_*))^{1/2}, one has 0 < epsilon < 1 and F(x_k) - F(x_*) <= (1 - epsilon)^k (F(x_0) - F(x_*)) for every k.

clauses.text: The explicit functions A,C,eta,rho,N just stated are closed functions of internally bound public problem parameters, with no future-run or hidden objective dependence.

nodes.statement: For internally bound inputs M,m,lambda,L,Delta,epsilon and fixed inner K define A=M+2/lambda, C=1+A+A^2*K^2/m+sqrt(A^4*(2A)^(3/2)*K^3*L*sqrt(Delta)/(6*m^5)), eta=1/(2*C), rho=m^2/(2*A*C), and N=ceil(2*A*C/m^2*log(max(1,Delta/epsilon))). The tuned method is exactly Algorithm2 with this eta; xstar is not an input.
